newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BONDS END UP ON INTL BULLISHNESS.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BONDS END UP ON INTL BULLISHNESS.

text.p: Bonds closed clearly up on
Thursday after bulls took U.S. Treasuries through resistance on
Wednesday, boosting Bunds, and as Finnish short end rate hike
fears eased on central bank comments, dealers said.
German rate woes were also easing, they said.
"This bull is hard to kill," said one.
FRA's maintained early gains posted after Bank of Finland
board member Matti Vanhala said the inflation mechanism may have
changed and that the tone in labour market rhetoric had been
moderate, dealers said. Early trade was lively, but summer calm
returned in the afternoon.
U.S. housing starts data reported in the afternoon was in
line with expectations but U.S. Treasuries weakened slightly
after the Finnish market close when the Philadelphia Fed survey
showed business activity at 28.1 in July versus a forecast
reading of 18.
Eyes were on U.S. export and import prices due at 1400/1100
GMT on Friday. The German IFO business climate will be reported
at 1100/0800 GMT, but one dealer said that even a stronger than
expected figure was unlikely to break the firm trend.
The markka was mostly steady after the Bank of Finland's
Vanhala said current forex rates were no problem.
